Rashi on Pesachim 97b:1:1.hebrew: לאחריות - שאם תאבד האחת, יביא חבירתה. והכא איכא לאקשויי: הא לאו אבודה היא? אלא דקא מותיב ליה קושיא אחריתי:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:1:1.english: As a guarantee - That if one is lost, he will bring its companion. And here one could ask: Surely it is not lost? Rather, [he did not ask this because] he raises another objection against him.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג והא אלו בפסח כי האי גוונא קרב שלמים - דהיינו מותר הפסח גמור, שהרי לכך הופרש, ואין כאן דחוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:2:1.english: We read: But if [it were] a Pesach [offering], in a case like this it is sacrificed as a peace-offering - For this is a complete remainder of the Pesach [offering], since it was set aside for that [purpose], and there is no [issue of] deferral here.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:2:2.hebrew: אלא - לא תיבעי רועה בחטאת היכא משכחת לה, דשמואל כר"ש ס"ל דאמר במסכת תמורה: חמש חטאות מתות — הנזכרות למיתה מתות הן בכל ענינים שאתה מוצא, וחטא' שכיפרו בעליה מתה בכל שהיא — בין שנמצאת קודם כפרה, בין שנמצאת לאחר כפרה, בין שהפרישה לאחריות — מתה הנותרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:2:2.english: Rather - Do not ask where you find a grazing [animal] in the case of a sin-offering, for Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said in Tractate Temurah: Five sin-offerings are left to die — those mentioned for death die in all circumstances that you find [them], and a sin-offering whose owners achieved atonement dies in whatever [case] it is — whether it was found before atonement, whether it was found after atonement, [or] whether he set it aside as security — the remaining one dies.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:3:1.hebrew: והא רועה לר' שמעון לית ליה - ומאי היא דקאמר שמואל, כל שבחטאת רועה:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:3:1.english: But Rabbi Shimon does not have [the case of] "left to graze" - And [so] what is it that Shmuel said: "Any [case] where in a sin-offering it is left to graze"?

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:3:2.hebrew: שמואל נמי חדא קאמר כל שבחטאת מתה - דהיינו כיפרו בעליה, מ"מ בפסח קרב שלמים, ותו לא אמר מידי. ועל כרחין, כיון דכל אבודין בפסח קריבין שלמים ושמואל חדא קאמר, מוקמי' לה כר"ש; דאי כר' או כרבנן דאית להו רועה בחטאת, מאי סימנא קא נקיט שמואל למימר חדא: כל שבחטאת מתה, בפסח קרב שלמים? הלא אף הרועה בחטאת קריבה שלמים בפסח! אבל השתא דס"ל כר"ש, הוי סימן שלם, דאין לך אבוד בחטאת שאינו מת ואין לך אבוד בפסח שאינו קרב:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:3:2.english: Shmuel also said [only] one [rule]: whatever in [the case of] a sin-offering is left to die - That is, [where] its owners atoned [with another offering], in any case with a Paschal offering it is offered as a peace-offering, and he said nothing further. And perforce, since all lost [animals] with a Paschal offering are offered as peace-offerings, and Shmuel said [only] one [rule], we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Shimon; for if [it were] in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] or in accordance with the Rabbis, who hold [there is a category of] left to graze with a sin-offering, what [sort of] rule is Shmuel adopting in stating [only] one [case]: "Whatever in [the case of] a sin-offering is left to die, in [the case of] a Paschal offering is offered as a peace-offering"? Behold, even that which is left to graze in [the case of] a sin-offering is offered as a peace-offering in [the case of] a Paschal offering! But now that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, it is a complete rule, for you have no lost [animal] in [the case of] a sin-offering that is not left to die, and you have no lost [animal] in [the case of] a Paschal offering that is not offered.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:1.hebrew: ומאי קא משמע לן - שמואל? כיון דכל אבודין בחטאת מתין, ואתא שמואל למימר כל אבודין בפסח קריבין שלמים — מתניתין היא: "הפסח שנמצא אחר שחיטה", ומתרצינן לה לעיל "אחר זמן שחיטה יקרב", אלמא קסבר: האבוד בחצות יקרב:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:1.english: And what does he teach us - [That is,] Shmuel? Since all lost [animals] in [the case of] a sin-offering are left to die, and Shmuel comes to say [that] all lost [animals] in [the case of] a Paschal offering are offered as peace-offerings — [this] is [already taught in] our Mishnah: "The Paschal lamb that was found after the slaughter," and we explained it above [as meaning that] after the time of slaughter it is offered; apparently, it holds [that] what is lost at midday is offered.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:2.english: To exclude [the opinion] of Rabbi Yochanan - Who disagrees with him and says: a Paschal lamb is offered as a peace-offering only when it is found after slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:3.hebrew: אבל נמצא קודם שחיטה - ואע"ג דאבוד היה בחצות, רועה, דשחיטת השניה קבעה ליה לקמא בדחוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:3.english: But [if it was] found before slaughter - Even though it was lost at midday, it grazes [until it develops a blemish], for the slaughter of the second [animal] establishes the first [one] as deferred.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:4.hebrew: קא משמע לן - שמואל דאמר כל שבחטאת מתה, וכר' שמעון דאמר אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה; ואשמעינן שמואל: אבוד בשעת הפרשה ובחצות, שהוא נקרא אבוד, אפי' נמצא קודם שחיטה קרב שלמים, דחצות הוא דקבעיה בדחוי. והשתא, אע"ג דאוקימנא לשמואל חדא קאמר, ליכא לאוקומא כל שבחטאת מתה אמתו לה בעליה, דהא כל מתו בעליה מתות, ואלו פסח מתו בעליו אחר חצות רועה וקבעתיה חצות, וליכא למימר דסביר' ליה שמואל חצות לא קבעה, דהא ר' יוחנן בר פלוגתיה הא סברא אית ליה. הלכך, על כרחיך באבודין מוקמינן ליה. ועוד, דר' יוחנן בר פלוגתיה אאבודין פליג, דקאמר נמצא:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:4:4.english: He teaches us - Shmuel, who said "any [case] in which a sin-offering is left to die [a Paschal lamb is offered as peace-offerings]," and [he holds] like Rabbi Shimon, who said [that a sin-offering that was] lost at the time of designation [of a replacement] is left to die; and Shmuel teaches us [regarding a Paschal lamb that was] lost at the time of designation and [still lost] at midday — for it is called "lost" — [that] even if it is found before slaughter, it is offered as peace-offerings, for it is midday that established it in [a state of] rejection. And now, even though we have established that Shmuel is stating [only] one [rule], one cannot establish "any [case] in which a sin-offering is left to die" as referring to [a case where] its owners died, because all [sin-offerings whose] owners died are left to die, whereas a Paschal lamb whose owners died after midday grazes, and [even though] midday established it; and one cannot say that Shmuel holds that midday does not establish [it], for Rabbi Yochanan, his disputant, holds that view. Therefore, perforce we establish [Shmuel's statement] as referring to lost [animals]. And furthermore, because Rabbi Yochanan, his disputant, disagrees regarding lost [animals], as he says "found."

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:5:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן לישנא אחרינא ואלו בפסח היכא דאבד ונמצא אחר חצות קודם שחיטה קרב שלמים - ולעיל קא מיהדר: "והרי אבודה בשעת הפרשה לרבנן וכו'", ואלו בפסח האבוד בחצות, והפריש אחר תחתיו, ונמצא זה אחר חצות — קרב שלמים, כר' זירא, ואע"ג דאבוד היה בשעת הפרשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:5:1.english: Thus we recite the text: Another version: Whereas with a Paschal lamb, where it was lost and found after midday, before slaughter, it is offered as a peace-offering - And [this version] refers back to [what was stated] above: "But behold, [a sin-offering] lost at the time of designation, according to the Rabbis, etc." — and whereas with a Paschal lamb that was lost at midday, and he designated another in its stead, and this [first] one was found after midday, it is offered as a peace-offering, in accordance with Rabbi Zeira, even though it was lost at the time of designation.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:5:2.hebrew: ומשני בלישנא אחרינא, שמואל כרבה סבירא ליה, דאמר קודם שחיטה שנינו, שהנמצא קודם שחיטה רועה בפסח, כרבנן בחטאת:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:5:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers in the other version: Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbah, who said [that] we taught "before slaughter," [meaning] that [an animal] that is found before slaughter grazes in the case of a Paschal lamb, like the Rabbis [hold] in the case of a sin-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:6:1.hebrew: ופרכינן והא מדאמר ר' יוחנן עלה אין הפסח קרב שלמים אלא שנמצא אחר שחיטה - מכלל דשמואל אמר אפילו נמצא קודם שחיטה קרב שלמים, דלאו שחיטה קבעה אלא חצות קבעה, וזה כיון דבחצות אבוד היה, קרב שלמים. אלמא לשמואל, אבוד בשעת הפרשה אע"פ שהיה בשעת כפרה, קרב שלמים:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:6:1.english: And we ask: But from the fact that Rabbi Yoḥanan said about it [that] a Paschal lamb is sacrificed as a peace-offering only when it was found after slaughter - By inference, Shmuel said [that] even if it was found before slaughter, it is sacrificed as a peace-offering, because slaughter does not determine [its status]; rather, midday determines [it]. And this [animal], since it was lost at midday, is sacrificed as a peace-offering. Apparently, according to Shmuel, [an animal] lost at the time of designation [of the replacement], even though it was [found] at the time of atonement, is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:7:1.hebrew: אלא שמואל כר' סבירא ליה - כדלעיל, עד "קא משמע לן חצות קבע":
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:7:1.english: Rather, Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] - As [explained] above, up to "it teaches us that midday determines [its status]."

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:8:1.english: Or a male two years old - For it is not fit for a Paschal [offering].

Rashi on Pesachim 97b:8:2.hebrew: ירעה עד שיסתאב ויביא בדמיו שלמים - דקבעתיה הפרשה, אע"פ שמעיקרו דחוי הוא, הרי הוא כקבוע שנדחה, שאין הוא עצמו קרב שלמים אלא דמיו:
Rashi on Pesachim 97b:8:2.english: It is left to graze until it becomes unfit, and he brings peace-offerings with its money - Because the designation fixed [sanctity upon] it, even though from the outset it is rejected [from being offered], it is like a fixed [offering] that became rejected, so that it itself is not offered as a peace-offering, rather its money [is].

Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:1:1.hebrew: כדרבי אושעיא דאמר הפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות כו' - מה שפרש"י דהוה מצי לאקשויי: "והא לא אבוד הוא", אלא דאקשי' קושיא אחריתי — לא נהירא, דאין זה סוגיית הגמרא; דאמאי דפריך שמואל "רועה באבודה היכי משכחת לה", לא משני מידי במאי דקאמר "כדר' אושעיא". ונראה לר"י דרבי אושעיא דקאמר "השניה תרעה", בכל ענין קאמר, ואפי' אבדה אחר כך; דלא דמיא לשאר אבודין דמתין לרבי, דשאר אבודין תחלת הפרשתן להקרבה, וכשאבדו נדחו מהקרבה, ובדין הוא שימותו; אבל מפריש ב' חטאות לאחריות, דתחלת הפרשתן לדחוי, כמו שרועה בלא אבדה — הכי נמי באבדה. אי נמי איכא למימר, דאפילו לא אבדה חשיב כאבדה: הואיל וכשמפרישה לא חזיא להקרבה, חשיב לה אבודה. ולא דמיא לאבודת לילה, דהתם לא נדחת בשעה הראוי' להקרבה, והוי כאילו כל שעה ראוי' להקרבה; אבל הכא איכא חדא ודאי דלא קרבה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:1:1.english: "In accordance with Rabbi Oshaya, as [Rabbi Oshaya] said: If one separated two sin-offerings as a guarantee, etc." - That which Rashi explained, that [the Gemara] could have objected: "But this is not a lost [sin-offering]!" rather it raised a different objection — this does not appear [correct], for this is not the flow of the Gemara; because regarding that which [the Gemara] asked [against] Shmuel, "How can you find a grazing [sin-offering] in a lost [case]?", [the Gemara] would not have answered anything at all by saying "In accordance with Rabbi Oshaya." And it appears to the Ri that when Rabbi Oshaya says "the second is left to graze," he states it in every case, even if it was lost afterward; for it is not similar to other lost [sin-offerings] that die according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], since other lost [sin-offerings] are initially separated for sacrifice, and when they are lost they are rejected from sacrifice, and by right they must die; however, [when] one separates two sin-offerings as a guarantee, since their initial separation is for rejection, just as it grazes without having been lost, so too [it grazes even] when it was lost. Alternatively, one can say that even if it was not lost, it is considered like a lost [sin-offering]: since at the time he separates it, it is not fit for sacrifice, it is considered lost. And it is not similar to [a sin-offering] lost at night, for there it was not rejected at a time fit for sacrifice, and it is as though every hour is fit for sacrifice; but here, there is certainly one that will not be sacrificed.

Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:1:2.hebrew: הפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות - קשה לריב"א: היכי דמי? אי דאמר "הרי זו חטאת" וחזר ואמר "הרי זו חטאת", אין קדושה חל על השניה, דאין אדם מביא שתי חטאות על חטא אחד. ואי דאמר "הרי אלו בהמות חטאות", האמר רבה במי שהוציאוהו (עירובין ד' נ.): כל שאינו בזה אחר זה, אפי' בבת אחת אינו, ואפי' אחת מהן לא קדשה! וע"כ אית לן למימר כגון שאמר: אחת מהן תהא חטאת, והאחרת לאחריות. וקשה לן: בשלא נאבדה החטאת אחת, אמאי שני' תרע'? והא לא הוקדשה אלא לאחריות החטאת, דהיינו אם תאבד; אבל אם לא נאבדה, לא נתקדשה! ונראה לר"י דכל כי האי גוונא גמירי לה דרועה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:1:2.english: [If] one separated two sin-offerings as a guarantee - Riba has a difficulty: What is the case? If he said, "Behold, this is a sin-offering," and then went back and said, "Behold, this [other one] is a sin-offering," sanctity does not take effect upon the second one, for a person cannot bring two sin-offerings for one sin. And if he said, "Behold, these are sin-offering animals," didn't Rabbah say in [the chapter] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (Eruvin 50a): Anything that is not [effective] sequentially is not [effective] even simultaneously — and [thus] not even one of them would become consecrated! Perforce we must say [it is] a case where he said: "One of them shall be a sin-offering, and the other as a guarantee." Yet we still have a difficulty: when the one sin-offering is not lost, why is the second [animal] left to graze? After all, it was consecrated only as a guarantee for the sin-offering, meaning if it gets lost; but if it does not get lost, it was never consecrated! And it appears to Ri that in any such case, it is a received tradition that it is left to graze.

Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:2:1.hebrew: אלא שמואל כר' שמעון סביר' ליה - פרש"י: דאי כרבי, מאי סימנא דנקיט שמואל? הלא אף הרועה בחטאת, בפסח קריבה שלמים! ולא נהירא לר"י, דמאי קאמר? הא באבודה לא משכחת לרבי דרועה, דבהפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות פירש רש"י גופיה דלאו אבוד הוא. ומיהו לפירוש ר"י, דפירש דר' אושעיא מיירי אפי' באבודה, אתי שפיר. ונראה לר"י, דכר' שמעון נמי לא מתוקם אלא באבודין; דאם לא כן, תיקשי דנאבד קודם חצות ונמצא קודם חצות בפסח רועה, ואבודת לילה דלאו אבודה (היא) בפסח, קודם חצות מתה לרבי שמעון. ואע"ג דלרבי שמעון אית ליה לקמן (פסחים ד' צח.) בעלי חיים אינן נדחין, וסבירא ליה בפסח [דמית] אחר חצות קרב שלמים אע"פ שנדחה — שמואל לא קסבר לה בהא כר' שמעון. ורשב"ם מפרש, דהא דשנינן "כי קאמר שמואל באבודין, בדחויין לא אמר" — שנויא דחיקא הוא. והשתא דמשני סבר לה כרבי שמעון, מתרץ מילתיה דשמואל כמשמעות הראשון, דמיירי בין באבודין בין בדחויין. והשתא לא מצי שמואל סבר כרבי, דאם כן קשיא חטאת שעברה שנתה והפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות, דלרבי לאו למיתה אזלי, ובפסח קריבה שלמים. הלכך מוקי לה כרבי שמעון, דאמר בכל חמש חטאות דלמיתה אזלי בכל ענין, ואילו בפסח קרבי שלמים. ואע"ג דנאבד ונמצא קודם חצות בפסח רועה לשמואל, דהא קתני לה בהדיא במתני' — מיהו חד צד באבד קרב שלמים, כגון נמצא אחר חצות. וה"ק: בכל ענין שבחטאת מתה, איכא צד דבפסח קרב שלמים. וקא משמע לן לאפוקי מדרבי יוחנן, דבע"א לא הוה קמשמע לן מידי, דבענינים אחרים מיתנו או במשנה או בברייתא דקרב שלמים. ואין ר"י יודע מנא ליה לגמרא דלר' שמעון חמש חטאות מתות בכל ענין. ויש לדקדק מדקתני בפרק שני דתמורה (דף טו.): "רבי שמעון אומר: חמש חטאות מתות, ולד חטאת, תמורת חטאת כו'", ולא מפליג כדמפליג בריש ולד חטאת (תמורה דף כא:) במתני' באבדה, בין כיפרו הבעלים ללא כיפרו; ואיהו לא מפליג לא בהא ולא באחריני — משמע דבכל ענין קאמר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:2:1.english: Rather, Shmuel held in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Rashi explained: For if [Shmuel held] like Rabbi, what distinction is Shmuel holding onto? Behold, even [the case of] grazing in a sin-offering is offered as a peace-offering in [the case of] a Paschal lamb! However, this does not seem right to Ri, for what is [Rashi] saying? Behold, in [the case of] a lost [sin-offering] you do not find according to Rabbi that it grazes, for regarding "one who separated two sin-offerings as a guarantee," Rashi himself explained that it is not [considered] lost. However, according to the explanation of Ri, who explained that Rabbi Oshaya is speaking even about a lost [animal], it works out well. And it appears to Ri that according to Rabbi Shimon as well, [Shmuel's statement] is only established regarding lost [animals]; for if not so, it would be difficult: for [a Paschal lamb] lost before midday and found before midday grazes in [the case of] a Paschal lamb, whereas [a sin-offering] lost at night — which is not [treated as] lost in [the case of] a Paschal lamb — dies before midday according to Rabbi Shimon. And even though Rabbi Shimon holds later (Pesachim 98a) that living animals are not [permanently] deferred, and he holds regarding a Paschal lamb [whose owner died] after midday that it is offered as a peace-offering even though it was deferred — Shmuel does not hold like Rabbi Shimon in this [matter]. And Rashbam explains that what we answered [earlier], "When Shmuel spoke, [he spoke] regarding lost [animals]; regarding deferred [animals] he did not speak," is a forced answer. And now that [the Gemara] answers [that Shmuel] holds like Rabbi Shimon, it resolves Shmuel's statement according to the initial understanding, that he is speaking both about lost [animals] and about deferred [animals]. And now Shmuel cannot hold like Rabbi, for if so, there would be a difficulty from a sin-offering whose year has passed and from one who separated two sin-offerings as a guarantee, which according to Rabbi do not go to death, yet in [the case of] a Paschal lamb it is offered as a peace-offering. Therefore, [the Gemara] establishes it according to Rabbi Shimon, who says regarding all five sin-offerings that they go to death in every case, whereas in [the case of] a Paschal lamb they are offered as peace-offerings. And even though [a Paschal lamb] that was lost and found before midday grazes in [the case of] a Paschal lamb according to Shmuel — for the Mishnah teaches this explicitly — nevertheless, [there is] one aspect in [the case of] a lost [animal where] it is offered as a peace-offering, such as [when it was] found after midday. And this is what [Shmuel] is saying: In every case where in [the case of] a sin-offering it dies, there is an aspect where in [the case of] a Paschal lamb it is offered as a peace-offering. And [Shmuel] informs us [of this] to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Yochanan; for otherwise, he would not be informing us of anything, since in the other cases they were already taught either in a Mishnah or in a Baraita that it is offered as a peace-offering. And Ri does not know from where the Gemara [knows] that according to Rabbi Shimon the five sin-offerings die in every case. And one can infer [this] from what is taught in the second chapter of Temurah (15a): "Rabbi Shimon says: Five sin-offerings die: the offspring of a sin-offering, the substitute of a sin-offering, etc.," and he does not distinguish as [the Tanna] distinguishes at the beginning of [the chapter] Velad Chatat (Temurah 21b) in the Mishnah regarding a lost [sin-offering], between [where] the owners achieved atonement and [where] they did not achieve atonement; whereas he [Rabbi Shimon] does not distinguish, neither in this nor in the other [cases] — [which] implies that he speaks in every case.

Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:8:1.hebrew: המפריש נקבה לפסחו כו' ויביא בדמיה שלמים - אומר ר"ת, דהא דקתני "ויביא בדמיה שלמים", היינו בשנשתיירה אחר הפסח, כמו כולה בבא דלעיל; אבל קודם הפסח — יביא בדמיה פסח. וכן מחלק בהדיא בברייתא בתמורה באלו קדשים (תמורה דף יט.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:8:1.english: One who separates a female for his Paschal lamb, etc., "and he shall bring peace-offerings with its money" - Rabbeinu Tam says that that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "and he shall bring peace-offerings with its money," refers to [a case] where it remained after Passover, like the entire previous clause; however, before Passover, he brings a Paschal lamb with its money. And so [the Tanna] explicitly distinguishes in a baraita in Temurah, in [the chapter] Eilu Kodashim (Temurah 19a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:8:2.hebrew: ויביא בדמיה שלמים - אבל היא עצמה אינה קריבה שלמים, דיש דחוי בדמים, כדאמר בגמרא, שמתחלה לא הוקדשה ליקרב היא עצמה. וא"ת: ימכרנה כמות שהיא בלא מום, כיון שמעולם לא נתקדשה קדושת הגוף? ואור"י: דלא מיבעיא מקדיש נקבה לפסחו — דפסח קרב שלמים אחר הפסח, והיא ראויה לשלמים אם תחלה הוקדשה לכך — אלא אפי' מקדיש נקבה לאשמו אמר באלו קדשים (שם:): "תרעה עד שתסתאב ותימכר ויביא אשם". ואפילו רבי שמעון דאמר התם "תימכר שלא במום", מצי מודה הכא, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Pesachim 97b:8:2.english: "And he shall bring peace-offerings with its proceeds" - But [the animal] itself is not offered as a peace-offering, because there is rejection with respect to monetary [consecration], as it states in the Gemara, since from the outset it was not consecrated to be offered itself. And if you will say: Let him sell it as it is, without a blemish, since it was never consecrated with physical sanctity? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says: Not only [is this the case for] one who consecrates a female for his Paschal offering — for a Paschal offering is offered as a peace-offering after Pesach, and [a female] is fit for a peace-offering had it initially been consecrated for that — rather, even [for] one who consecrates a female for his guilt-offering, it states in [chapter] Eilu Kodashim (ibid. [Temurah 19b]): "It shall graze until it becomes blemished, and be sold, and he shall bring a guilt-offering [with the proceeds]." And even Rabbi Shimon, who says there, "It may be sold without a blemish," can agree here, as I have explained.
